article.headline: EOG Resources' Earnings Jump 109.3% As Oil Producer Trades Near High
article.deck: EOG is in the buy range of a four-week flat base, 2.4% past the 154.26 buy point, with the range running to 161.97.
body: EOG Resources explores for and produces crude oil, natural gas liquids and natural gas, mostly in U.S. producing basins, with operations in Trinidad and Tobago and elsewhere. It also gathers, processes and markets what it pumps. The Houston company, incorporated in 1985, was once known as Enron Oil & Gas. Today it is one of the leaders of the energy group, the third-strongest group on the desk's list, alongside ConocoPhillips, Chevron and Occidental.

The case starts with the quarters. EOG earned 5.15 a share in the June quarter, up 109.3% from a year earlier, as revenue rose 58.6% to $8.49 billion. The trend is the point: EPS went from 2.70 in the September 2025 quarter to 1.30 in December, then 3.70 in March and 5.15 in June. Revenue dipped from $5.73 billion to $5.65 billion over the first two of those quarters, then rose to $6.76 billion and $8.49 billion, two straight quarters of sharp sequential gains.

The market is not paying much for that growth. EOG carries a market value of about $82.9 billion and trades at 9.7 times forward earnings and 12.3 times trailing earnings. The next report is due Nov. 5.

The stock has done the work. Shares are up 50.4% this year and 49.0% over 12 months, and EOG ranks 84 of 99 on the desk's list, though its RS line sits 12.8% below its high. It closed Thursday at 157.96, up 8 cents, while the S&P 500 fell 1.2%. Volume was light at 0.74 times the 50-day average.

On the chart, EOG broke out Oct. 14 from a four-week flat base with a 154.26 buy point. The base corrected 10.9% from a Sept. 15 high to a Sept. 30 low. Volume on the breakout ran 0.82 times average. Six sessions later the stock trades 2.4% above the buy point, inside a buy range that runs to 161.97. It hit a new 52-week high of 160.31 and closed 1.5% below it.
The trend is orderly. EOG sits 7.4% above its 50-day line at 147.13 and 16.7% above its 200-day line at 135.36. At 1.06 ATRs from the 21-day line, the stock is not stretched.

Headlines this week asked whether EOG is still cheap on strong earnings and a new 52-week high, and one said the stock may trade below fair value after its 113% run. Another discussed what its earnings beat means for shareholders.
article.watch: Watch whether EOG holds above the 154.26 buy point into the Nov. 5 earnings report.

article.headline: Spotify Soars 11.1% As Paying Users Climb And Results Beat Estimates
article.deck: Spotify cleared a 576.10 buy point in a seven-week cup and closed inside the buy range that runs to 604.91.
body: Spotify Technology jumped 58.32, or 11.1%, to 583.66 after its earnings report Thursday, closing 1.3% above the 576.10 buy point of a seven-week cup. The base ran 18.4% deep, from a Sept. 3 high to an Oct. 5 low, and the buy range extends to 604.91. Volume came in at 3.09 times the 50-day average. The cup formed after a bigger correction: the stock is still well below its Aug. 15, 2025, high of 748.30 and only climbed off a Feb. 5 low of 405.00.

Shares sit 16.3% below the 52-week high of 696.95. The close stands 11.3% above the 50-day line at 524.29 and 1.8 ATRs from the 21-day line, which leaves the trend intact rather than stretched. Relative strength lags: Spotify ranks 68 of 99 on the desk's list and its RS line trades 25.6% below its high. The stock is up 0.5% this year and down 15.3% over the past 12 months.

The quarters table is reported in euros. June-quarter revenue rose 13.9% to 4.78 billion euros. Earnings per share came to 2.61 euros, down from 3.45 in the March quarter and 4.43 in the December quarter, so profit has slipped two quarters running while sales grew. The stock trades at 33.9 times forward earnings.

Headlines Thursday said Spotify "turns up volume on paying users, beats estimates," and another framed the post-earnings gain as an example of how the AI trade has shifted. In after-hours trading the stock eased 0.6% to 580.09 as of 5:40 p.m. ET.
A close back under 576.10 would turn the move into a stalled breakout.
article.watch: Watch whether Spotify holds above the 576.10 buy point in the sessions after the report.

The stock has traded 92 sessions since its IPO. Its current two-week IPO base shows a 176.52 buy point and a 20.3% depth, and Thursday's close sits 18.0% below that buy point, near the base's 140.66 low. The base formed after a bigger correction: the stock is still 35.8% below its June 16 high of 225.64, set early in its trading life, and it bottomed at 104.83 on Aug. 3.

The close is 2.9% below the 50-day line at 149.12 and 5.3% below the 21-day line at 152.93. It reads 0.0 ATRs from the 21-day line, meaning the session's range reached the line before the selling took hold. The stock ranks 77 of 99 on the desk's list, but its RS line is 32.9% below its high. It is down 2.4% over the past month and up 25.8% over three months.

SpaceX lost 9 cents a share in the June quarter on revenue of $7.81 billion. The quarter before, it lost 41 cents on $4.69 billion. The payload gives no year-over-year growth rates. Market value stands near $1.91 trillion, at 66.9 times forward earnings.

Headlines said the earnings beat sparked profit-taking, that Musk wants to merge SpaceX and Tesla, and that a lawsuit alleges its booming data center business is fueled by illegal turbines. Another said Google pays SpaceX $11 billion a year for compute. After hours, the stock rose 1.2% to 146.50.

body: Regeneron gained 13.42, or 1.7%, to 819.09, bouncing off its 50-day line. Volume ran 1.24 times the 50-day average. The stock is building a seven-week cup with an 859.44 buy point, 10 cents above its 52-week high of 859.34. The cup corrected 16.0% from a Sept. 3 high to an Oct. 5 low, and the close sits 4.7% below the buy point. The buy range would run to 902.41.

The stock closed 3.5% above the 50-day line at 791.39 and 5.0% above the 21-day line at 780.05, 0.92 ATRs from that line. Regeneron ranks 79 of 99 on the desk's list, and its RS line is 9.7% below its high. It has gained 24.9% over three months and 41.4% over 12 months.

Earnings per share slipped 4.5% to 12.23 in the June quarter while revenue rose 16.7% to $4.29 billion. EPS rebounded from 6.75 in the March quarter but stayed below the 13.62 posted in the September 2025 quarter. The stock trades at 13.0 times forward earnings, and the next report is due Oct. 30.

Recent headlines centered on Dupixent: one said a strong Dupixent trajectory anchors Regeneron's solid financial results, and another argued the company's real value may be hiding in its Dupixent profit share rather than Eylea.
A move through 859.44 would complete the cup; a close back under the 50-day line would undo the bounce.
article.watch: Watch the 859.44 buy point and the Oct. 30 earnings report.

market_note: The S&P 500 fell 1.2% to 7663.43 and closed 0.5% below its 50-day line, the Nasdaq composite dropped 2.6% to 26008.86 and sits 2.3% under its 50-day, and the Dow finished flat at 52867.98, 1.0% above its 50-day. The S&P 500 carries 4 distribution days over the last 25 sessions and the Nasdaq 3, with Thursday added to the Nasdaq's count. The desk's read stays at Market in correction. Leadership is narrow and defensive: eight names on the desk's list broke out this week, led by drugmakers Amgen, Eli Lilly and Pfizer plus software names ServiceNow and Monday.com, while only 12% of the AI chip group and 6% of the AI infrastructure group hold above their 50-day lines; after the close, Deckers fell 7.3%, Comfort Systems 6.2%, Western Digital 5.2% and Seagate 3.1%.
